evidence: This claim is supported by the study's data analysis.

claim: Subsoil prokaryotic community similarity was not linked with plant community dissimilarity within the temperate biota.
source: Moreover, subsoil prokaryotic community similarity was not linked with plant community dissimilarity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) and long-term environmental distance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the study's data analysis.

claim: Subsoil prokaryotic community similarity was not linked with long-term environmental distance within the temperate biota.
source: Moreover, subsoil prokaryotic community similarity was not linked with plant community dissimilarity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) and long-term environmental distance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the study's data analysis.

claim: Subsoil prokaryotic community similarity was correlated weakly with the short-term environmental distance based on the correlation test (R2 = 0.011) within the temperate biota.
source: It was correlated weakly with the short-term environmental distance based on the correlation test (R2 = 0.011) and SEM (r = −0.002).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis.

claim: Subsoil prokaryotic community similarity was correlated weakly with the short-term environmental distance based on SEM (r = −0.002) within the temperate biota.
source: It was correlated weakly with the short-term environmental distance based on the correlation test (R2 = 0.011) and SEM (r = −0.002).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural equation modeling results.

claim: Cases of no distance-decay relationship for microorganisms have been reported previously (Zhou et al., 2008; Cox et al., 2016; Davison et al., 2015).
source: Cases of no distance-decay relationship for microorganisms have also been reported previously (Zhou et al., 2008; Cox et al., 2016; Davison et al., 2015), possibly explained by factors like the paleogeographic history (Cox et al., 2016; Davison et al., 2015) and plant-dependent (Davison et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: No distance-decay relationship for microorganisms can possibly be explained by factors like the paleogeographic history (Cox et al., 2016; Davison et al., 2015).
source: Cases of no distance-decay relationship for microorganisms have also been reported previously (Zhou et al., 2008; Cox et al., 2016; Davison et al., 2015), possibly explained by factors like the paleogeographic history (Cox et al., 2016; Davison et al., 2015) and plant-dependent (Davison et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: No distance-decay relationship for microorganisms can possibly be explained by plant-dependent factors (Davison et al., 2015).
source: Cases of no distance-decay relationship for microorganisms have also been reported previously (Zhou et al., 2008; Cox et al., 2016; Davison et al., 2015), possibly explained by factors like the paleogeographic history (Cox et al., 2016; Davison et al., 2015) and plant-dependent (Davison et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Soil prokaryotic similarity exhibited a U-shape distribution pattern over geographic distance at a scale of up to 4000 km.
source: This study provides a systematical analysis of the spatial pattern of soil prokaryotic communities in the northern grassland of China. Soil prokaryotic similarity exhibited a U-shape distribution pattern over geographic distance at a scale of up to 4000 km.
evidence: This claim summarizes the main finding of the study.

claim: This finding overturns the well-accepted geographic distance-decay relationship.
source: This finding overturns the well-accepted geographic distance-decay relationship, which was still valid in the top- or subsoils within the alpine biota and only in the topsoil within the temperate biota.
evidence: This claim is an interpretation of the study's findings in the context of existing knowledge.

claim: Habitats far more apart when across biotas were more similarly as revealed by the U-shape pattern for short-term environmental variables over geographic distance.
source: Despite different climate and ecosystem types in the alpine and temperate biotas, habitats far more apart when across biotas were more similarly as revealed by the U-shape pattern for short-term environmental variables over geographic distance.
evidence: This claim is supported by the study's findings on short-term environmental variables.

claim: Deterministic processes were found to dominate the soil prokaryotic community assembly by null model and βNTI analyses.
source: Consistently, deterministic processes were found to dominate the soil prokaryotic community assembly by null model and βNTI analyses, and further partial Mantel analysis revealed that SWC and dissolved nutrients (DOC and DON) may be responsible for the decay relationship of prokaryotic community similarity over environmental distance, overturning the geographic distance-decay relationship.
evidence: This claim is supported by null model and βNTI analyses.

claim: SWC and dissolved nutrients (DOC and DON) may be responsible for the decay relationship of prokaryotic community similarity over environmental distance, overturning the geographic distance-decay relationship.
source: Consistently, deterministic processes were found to dominate the soil prokaryotic community assembly by null model and βNTI analyses, and further partial Mantel analysis revealed that SWC and dissolved nutrients (DOC and DON) may be responsible for the decay relationship of prokaryotic community similarity over environmental distance, overturning the geographic distance-decay relationship.
evidence: This claim is supported by partial Mantel analysis results.

source: A total of 258 samples were collected from the top- (0–5 cm in depth) and subsoils (5–20 cm in depth) in both the alpine biota on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and the temperate biota on the Inner Mongolia Plateau, China, on a scale up to 4000 km.
